I believe that automated deletion of empty subverses underestimates the value of emptiness, high-value subtext, and creative architecture (account names & links between subs) while simultaneously overlooking some arguably more worthy candidates for deletion (corporate/military propaganda subs, racist subs, etc.)

This could be construed as an issue of free speech (is holding up a blank sign not a form of expression?) Squatting has long been an activist tactic; you can read about this on wikipedia & elsewhere on the internet. Some subs (like /v/greatapes and /v/whiterights) have been squatted to keep them from being used for racist organizing and the circulation of racist propaganda. In these and other instances the value of squatting (especially for the site as a whole) has little or nothing to do with whether any posts have been made in the sub.

Often coming up with high-value subtext is a more valuable contribution for a moderator to make than posting content. Subtext can link users to resources and additional information about a subject, set the tone & backdrop for a community or a subject, connect users to other subverses on whoaverse, and more. As mods are solely responsible for subtext while in most instances anyone can post in a sub, a good moderator devoting attention to high-value subtext is doing a lot for their community, even if the sub remains empty, waiting for a community to fill it with content.

I am probably not the only user who has created a number of subs with their long-term potential to contribute to the growth and value of whoaverse in mind. Some of these are facing deletion very soon, and a lot of time and energy invested in whoaverse's future & growth could disappear without us having a larger discussion about the value of squatting and the problems with attempting to objectively measure a subverses' worth on the basis of whether or not it's empty.

If the ultimate end-goal of this rule was to make atko's job easier vis a vis take over requests, I would be more than happy to work with a group of users here to come up with a way that we, as a community, can take up (some of?) the responsibility in doing that. As the site grows it will surely become much more difficult if not impossible for one person to handle takeover requests so this is probably something that we would need to figure out anyway!

I wish I had more time to write this post but the concrete deadline of "deletion after 30 days" requires me to at least initiate this conversation now. For the most part I just wanted to start this discussion and maybe persuade atko to suspend automated deletion, at least temporarily, so that we have a chance to talk about this before a number of subverses with potential are deleted.

For what it's worth, whatever the merits of automatic deletion (after 30 days) yes/no in the abstract are, if there were any way that this policy could only be implemented for subs created after it was announced (9/16 or later) i would not mind making one post per sub in the future. It would be a huge relief because I wouldn't lose all of the work I've put into creating spaces for communities I believe have potential once whoaverse has more users.

i'm just a little confused as to why it's necessary to require a single post. When that's all it takes to circumvent automatic deletion then the only subs getting deleted are ones created before this policy was announced, and ones created by people who don't know or forget about this rule.
